A summary of the most recent Disparate Impact Analysis of such tool, as well as the distribution date of the tool to which the analysis applies, has been made publicly available on the website of the employer or employment agency prior to the implementation or use of such tool (Section 203-f 2 B).
4. The summary of the most recent Disparate Impact Analysis provided to the employer shall be reported to the Department at least annually (Section 203-f 2 C).

The Disparate Impact Analysis shall differentiate between candidates who were selected and candidates who were not selected by the tool and shall include a Disparate Impact Analysis as specified in the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures promulgated by the United States Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (Section 203-f 1 B).
answer_high_temp: According to the given context, 'Disparate Impact Analysis' is defined as an impartial analysis that assesses the likelihood of an adverse impact on any group based on sex, race, ethnicity, or other protected classes under Article Fifteen of the Executive Law. The analysis should differentiate between candidates who were selected and those who were not selected by the automated employment decision tool, and include a disparate impact analysis as specified in the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures promulgated by the United States Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. The analysis results should be reported to the employer implementing or using the automated employment decision tool. The analysis should be conducted at least annually and the summary of the most recent disparate impact analysis, along with the distribution date of the tool to which the analysis applies, must be made publicly available on the employer's website prior to the implementation or use of the tool.
